newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Horizon-Multiplan sees swinging to black.
newsitem.headline: Horizon-Multiplan sees swinging to black.

text.p: Hungarian R&D company Horizon-Multiplan Rt plans to swing to operating profit in 1997 from losses in 1996, the company's General Director, Csaba Elek, told shareholders on Wednesday.
The company sees an operating profit of 25 million forints in 1997, 313 million in 1998 and 660 million in 1999, after an operating loss of 97.5 million last year.

The company, which specialises in the R&D of humic acid products, based its hopes on a wider portfolio than the current one-product-portfolio, Elek said, adding that they regarded the Russian market as key to reach their target.
"Our main problem is that we have nothing to sell. Unless we establish a product portfolio, the unfavourable trend cannot be expected to be reversed," Elek said.

"Once Russian markets manage to bear results... and we manage to reach our aims also on the domestic market we can reach a profit of 25 million forints in 1997," he told the company's annual shareholders meeting.

Elek said the company on Wednesday signed a preliminary agreement to establish a production facility in Russia for the production of Horizon's human product. The start of the production is expected in October.
The company, which so far has produced only a health supplement that contains trace elements, plans to widen its product portfolio to include veterinary products as well.

Horizon-Multiplan has started to produce supplementary horse feed jointly with Hungary's Babolna-Phylaxia with Ireland's Cross Vetpharm Ltd taking over for distribution 18,000 bottles this year, Elek said.

Last year the company failed to meet its plans and on the domestic market sold only 115,000 bottles of its health supplement product instead of the planned 200,000 units, partly because what the company attributes to a bad distributing network it has since changed.
On the Budapest Stock Exchange Horizon-Multiplan shares closed unchanged at 300 forints.
